$comment: Ouro AX: the standard. Each claim is one checkable rule about an interface whose user is an agent. ax/xray.mjs checks every claim from outside, against any CLI, HTTP API or MCP server, without importing its code. Sources: Tandem's docs/ax-principles.md (P1-P15) and the Ouro UI design record of 2026-10-11 (the CLI kit and MCP kit lists).

claims.rule: `<cli> help --json` prints one JSON document that names every command.
claims.rationale: An agent learns the interface from the interface. Help that parses lets it list commands without scraping prose.
claims.source: Ouro UI 2026-10-11 CLI kit: help that parses; Tandem P15
claims.check: Run `help --json` (then `--help --json`). Pass when stdout is one JSON document with a `commands` array of objects that each have a `name`.
claims.fix: Keep help as data (a COMMANDS table) and print it with `help --json`: { commands: [{ name, effect, summary, usage[] }], exitCodes: [{ code, meaning }] }.

claims.rule: Help says who sees each command: only the person, or other people.
claims.rationale: The one thing an agent must know before acting is whether other people will see it.
claims.check: Each command in `help --json` has `effect` of `private` or `others`.
claims.fix: Add `effect: "private" | "others"` to every command in help JSON, from one action catalog, and group the text help under two headings.

claims.rule: Every command answers `<command> --help` with exit 0 on stdout, and nothing on stderr.
claims.rationale: An agent asks the command itself, at the point of use; it should not need a separate document.
claims.source: Ouro UI 2026-10-11 CLI kit; Tandem P7
claims.check: Run `<command> --help` for every listed command.
claims.fix: Route `<command> --help` to the command's own help page before parsing its arguments.

claims.rule: No help line is wider than the width limit (100 columns by default).
claims.rationale: Long lines wrap unpredictably in terminals and transcripts and cost tokens to re-read.
claims.check: Measure every line of `--help` and each `<command> --help`.
claims.fix: Wrap help at one width in the help renderer, not by hand.

claims.rule: The overview (`--help`) fits one screen: at most 60 lines.
claims.rationale: The overview is read on every cold start; details belong on each command's page.
claims.check: Count the lines of `--help`.
claims.fix: Keep one line per command in the overview and move details to `<command> --help`.

claims.rule: Exit codes are documented, and every exit code the CLI gives is one of them.
claims.rationale: Stable, documented exit codes let an agent branch without parsing prose.
claims.source: Ouro UI 2026-10-11 CLI kit: stable exit codes
claims.check: Read `exitCodes` from help JSON (or an `Exit codes:` line), then compare every exit code seen during the X-ray.
claims.fix: Keep one exit-code table, print it in help and help JSON, and exit only with codes from it.

claims.rule: Every read takes `--json` and prints exactly one JSON document (a stream prints JSON lines), exits 0 and writes nothing to stderr.
claims.rationale: One parseable answer per call is the cheapest thing for an agent to consume.
claims.source: Ouro UI 2026-10-11 CLI kit: one definition gives human output and --json; Tandem help: --json on every read
claims.check: Run each read command's argument-free usage (or with one harvested ref) with `--json`.
claims.fix: Give the read a `--json` that prints the same data the text shows, as one document.

claims.rule: An unknown command fails with the usage exit code and lists the commands.
claims.rationale: A guessed command is the commonest first call; the error should be the menu.
claims.check: Run a command that does not exist.
claims.fix: On an unknown command, print one line: `unknown command "x". Commands: a, b, c. Details: <cli> help`, and exit with the usage code.

claims.rule: An unknown flag fails before anything runs, and the error names the flag.
claims.rationale: A silently ignored flag gives an agent a wrong answer that looks right: `--limt 2` returns everything.
claims.check: Run a read with a flag no command has, and with a misspelt real flag.
claims.fix: Check every flag against the command's declared flags before acting; refuse an unknown one with the usage exit code.

claims.rule: A misspelt flag's error names the closest real flag.
claims.rationale: The error should carry the fix, so the next call is right.
claims.source: Ouro UI 2026-10-11 CLI kit: errors that name the fix
claims.check: Run a read with one of its flags misspelt (a letter dropped).
claims.fix: Suggest the declared flag nearest by edit distance: `unknown flag --limt; did you mean --limit?`.

claims.rule: A command missing a required argument fails with the usage exit code and says what to give.
claims.rationale: The error is where the agent learns the argument; it should not have to open help.
claims.check: Run each command whose every usage needs an argument with no arguments.
claims.fix: Validate arguments first and name the missing one and where to get it.

claims.rule: Every error is one line on stderr, with nothing on stdout.
claims.rationale: One line is cheap to read and easy to quote back; stdout stays parseable.
claims.check: Every failing call the X-ray makes.
claims.fix: Catch errors at the entry point and print one line to stderr.

claims.rule: Every error names a next action: a command to run or a flag to add.
claims.rationale: An agent recovers from the error alone when the error says what to do instead.
claims.source: Tandem P7, P8; Ouro UI 2026-10-11: errors that name the fix
claims.check: Every failing call's error line contains `<cli> <word>`, a `--flag`, or a quoted command name.
claims.fix: End each error with what to do: `Try "<cli> conversations"`.

claims.rule: No call prints a stack trace.
claims.rationale: A stack trace is noise to an agent and leaks internals.
claims.check: Look for `    at ` frames in every output.
claims.fix: Turn the thrown error into a one-line message at the entry point.

claims.rule: Ambiguous verbs (edit, delete, remove) don't act; they answer with the specific commands.
claims.rationale: `edit` could mean a private draft or a message others already saw; guessing is how agents do the wrong thing.
claims.check: Run `edit`, `delete` and `remove` when they are not listed commands. Pass when each fails and names at least one listed command.
claims.fix: Answer each ambiguous verb with one line naming the private command and the one others see.

claims.rule: Every command other people see refuses to run without `--why`, and says so.
claims.rationale: What others see is logged with who asked and why.
claims.check: Run each others-see command with a made-up target and no `--why`.
claims.fix: Check `--why` first in every others-see command and refuse with the usage exit code.

claims.rule: A wrong reference fails before anything reaches anyone, and the error says where to get a right one.
claims.rationale: Checking before acting keeps a stale id from becoming a wrong message.
claims.check: Run each others-see command with `--why` and a target that does not exist.
claims.fix: Resolve the target first; on a miss, name the command that lists valid ones.

claims.rule: Every command other people see has a preview that acts on nothing (`--dry-run`) and names who will see it.
claims.rationale: An agent, or a checker, can confirm the audience without acting; a wall it is not, because nothing waits on it.
claims.source: Tandem P4; the Apple Developer AX candidate (dry-run plans)
claims.check: When `<command> --help` mentions `--dry-run`, run it on a real target with `--why`. Pass when it exits 0, names who will see it, and nothing changes.
claims.fix: Add `--dry-run`: resolve the target, print the preview line ("Would send to X as the person. Everyone in X will see it."), exit 0, and send nothing.

claims.rule: A command that takes free text accepts it as one argument, not only on stdin, and its help shows that form.
claims.rationale: An agent allowed to run only this CLI (`shell(<cli>)`) cannot pipe into it: the pipe's first command is not the CLI, so the call is denied.
claims.source: ax-eval baseline of Tandem main, 2026-10-30: every T3 and T4 run's `printf … | m365tandem send/edit-sent … -` was denied
claims.check: For each usage that reads text from stdin (`-`), look for a usage of the same command with a placeholder in that place. For a command others see that offers --dry-run, the preview probe passes the text as an argument.
claims.fix: Accept the text as an argument and list that usage first; keep `-` for stdin.

claims.rule: A wait command accepts the refs the reads list: `watch <ref>` waits on the conversation a list gave.
claims.rationale: Waiting through the interface beats polling; when the wait refuses the ref the agent holds, agents fall back to blind streams and pollers.
claims.source: ax-eval baseline of Tandem main, 2026-10-30: T5 runs tried `watch r82dfi` and `watch conversation:r82dfi` (exit 2), then a bare stream or a Python poller
claims.check: When the CLI has a `watch` or `wait` command, run it on a harvested conversation ref with a short timeout. Pass on exit 0 or the documented waited-and-nothing-happened code; fail on a usage error.
claims.fix: Let the wait take every ref a read prints, and exit with a documented code when nothing happens in time.

claims.rule: Reads change nothing.
claims.rationale: An agent must be able to look freely.
claims.check: Snapshot the state commands before and after every read the X-ray makes (including the flag probes); compare.
claims.fix: Keep reads free of writes (no mark-read, no log row, no cache eviction others see).

claims.rule: A refused call changes nothing, except an audit record that says it was refused.
claims.rationale: An agent that gets the call wrong must be able to try again safely.
claims.check: Snapshot the state commands around each refused probe of what other people see. Pass when nothing changed, or when every added record mentions the refusal and nothing was removed.
claims.fix: Refuse before writing anything; if you log the refusal, say so in the record (`send.refused`).

claims.rule: Every route answers JSON, with a JSON content type.
claims.rationale: One format, always parseable.
claims.check: GET every read route in the manifest.
claims.fix: Answer every route through one sendJson.

claims.rule: Every error is a JSON object with a string `error`.
claims.rationale: One error shape lets an agent handle every failure the same way.
claims.source: Ouro UI 2026-10-11 MCP kit: one error shape
claims.check: Every non-2xx answer the X-ray gets.
claims.fix: Throw one HttpError type and serialise it as { error, code? }.

claims.rule: Every error names a next action: a route, a field, or a command.
claims.rationale: `not found` alone leaves the agent guessing.
claims.check: Every non-2xx answer's `error` contains a route (`/api/...`), a quoted field, or a CLI command.
claims.fix: Say where to go: `no such conversation; GET /api/conversations lists them`.

claims.rule: The API's base path answers an index of its routes.
claims.rationale: An agent finds the routes from the API itself, not from source code.
claims.source: Tandem P15; Ouro UI 2026-10-11: discoverable capabilities
claims.check: GET the manifest's base path. Pass when it answers JSON naming at least 80% of the manifest's routes.
claims.fix: Serve GET /api with { routes: ["GET /api/x", ...] } from the same table the router uses.

claims.rule: An unknown route answers 404 and says where the routes are listed.
claims.rationale: A guessed route is the commonest first call.
claims.check: GET a route that does not exist.
claims.fix: Answer 404 with `no route GET /api/x; GET /api lists the routes`.

claims.rule: A route given an id that does not exist fails and says where to get a right one.
claims.rationale: Checking before acting keeps a stale id from becoming a wrong write.
claims.check: GET each `{id}` route with a made-up id; POST each others-see probe with a made-up target and a why.
claims.fix: On a miss, name the route that lists valid ids.

claims.rule: Every route that does what other people see refuses a request without a why, and names the field.
claims.rationale: What others see is logged with who asked and why.
claims.check: POST each others-see probe from the manifest without its why field.
claims.fix: Check the why field first and answer 4xx naming it.

claims.rule: GET requests change nothing.
claims.rationale: An agent must be able to look freely.
claims.check: Snapshot the manifest's state routes before and after every GET; compare.
claims.fix: Keep GET handlers free of writes.

claims.rule: A refused request changes nothing, except an audit record that says it was refused.
claims.rationale: An agent that gets the request wrong must be able to try again safely.
claims.check: Snapshot the manifest's state routes around each refused probe. Pass when nothing changed, or when every added record mentions the refusal and nothing was removed.
claims.fix: Refuse before writing anything; if you log the refusal, say so in the record.

claims.rule: The server lists its tools, each with a description and an input schema.
claims.rationale: The tool list is the MCP surface's help.
claims.check: initialize, then tools/list.
claims.fix: Give every tool a one-line description and a JSON Schema for its input.

claims.rule: Every tool says whether it only reads or changes something (`readOnlyHint` or `destructiveHint`).
claims.rationale: The MCP form of `effect`: who sees it.
claims.check: Read `annotations` from tools/list.
claims.fix: Set `annotations.readOnlyHint` on reads and `destructiveHint` on what others see.

claims.rule: A call missing a required argument is refused, and the error names the argument.
claims.rationale: Schemas that reject bad calls with the fix.
claims.check: Call each tool that has required arguments with none.
claims.fix: Validate input against the schema before running and name each missing field.

claims.rule: An unknown tool is refused, and the error names the tools or tools/list.
claims.rationale: The error should be the menu.
claims.check: Call a tool that does not exist.
claims.fix: Answer with the tool names.
